evals.name: new-plan-events
evals.prompt: Write the QA test plan for story KING-99001 (https://kinoadev.atlassian.net/browse/KING-99001): events via the AI agent — the kinoa_event_* tools (list, create, update, status, hide, delete, export). Acceptance criteria: an agent can list a game's events with name/type/status/hidden filters and paging; create an event with typed custom parameters; update its editable attributes and full parameter set; activate or deactivate it; hide or unhide it; delete it; export it to another game the caller can write to. Interview answers: Fixed test data (this is a skill eval: these are the fictional values of fixed-data.md, used on purpose — take them literally and do not query them): P1 = 7d3e1c2a-5b64-4f80-9a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b, Widget sandbox; P2 = 7d3e1c2b-6c75-4a91-8b2c-3d4e5f6a7b8c, Widget sandbox 2 (same company as P1); PLAYER1 = p_8f2a1c77 and PLAYER2 = p_3c9d0e14, both in P1 only; COMPANY = 7d3e1c2c-7d86-4ba2-9c3d-4e5f6a7b8c9d (the company of P1 and P2); ADMIN_API = https://mcp-test.example.com/internal/mcp-admin/api. Keep all artifacts; delete semantics unknown, assume soft; irreversible: none known; two checkpoints; one replica, writes enabled; roles per roles.yml; the kinoa-mcp source is open in this chat; no known issues and no earlier runs. The branch is up to date, do not ask about it. Do not call any tool of a Kinoa MCP connector.
evals.expected_output: A new file, in <scratch home>/.kinoa-qa/mcp/plans/, KING-99001-events-test-plan.md (version 1) in the fixed layout: header lines, §0 with the literal fixture values from the prompt and an artifacts table with real NAME/KEY-stamped names, §1 pointers plus domain facts only, §1.1 hypotheses wired to case ids, Part A tool sections in the fixed verb order with stable ids, §Grey, §Hand-off, Part B checkpoints as complete user_role states each with its admin-role-API request block, REPORT pointer; check-layout.sh passes.
assertions: The file is named KING-99001-events-test-plan.md, sits in <scratch home>/.kinoa-qa/mcp/plans/, and its header says **Plan version:** 1, **Earlier runs:** none and **Checked against:** commit <sha>

§0 carries exactly the fixture values of the prompt (Widget sandbox 7d3e1c2a-5b64-4f80-9a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b, Widget sandbox 2 7d3e1c2b-6c75-4a91-8b2c-3d4e5f6a7b8c, p_8f2a1c77, p_3c9d0e14) with no <…> placeholder and no empty cell, and no connector call was made to find or check them

Every case row is a three-column Id | Call | Expected row with full JSON arguments, every id has the shape pre-NN, <tool>-<kind>-NN, grey-NN, handoff-NN or role-<tool>-NN, every Expected cell opens with the one assertion that grades the case (per step when there are several) with anything more after the literal label `Also record:`, every count is relative to a BASE_ handle or scoped to NAME/KEY (never an absolute number), and every gap and grey-NN id appears in §1.1 or in the REPORT section's AC list

§A0 opens with one tools/list case per story tool (the seven kinoa_event_* tools), in the story's order and with the story's names; nothing comes before them; a pre- case records USER_ID from kinoa_system_ping and the next pre- case sends the admin role API GET and records ROLES_BEFORE
Part A tool sections follow the verb order list, create, update, lifecycle (status, hide), delete, export, and inside each section the kinds follow ok, sem, schema, rule, gap, iso

Every one of the seven tools has at least one ok case in its own section; kinoa_event_delete, kinoa_event_status and kinoa_event_hide each have sem cases — for delete and status the determination as a run of consecutive sem cases of at most five steps each, chained by Record values (_get, the unfiltered listing paged to the end, every status filter and all together, an untouched twin), for hide the round-trip through the hidden filter (hidden=true lists it, the default listing does not, unhide restores it)
§1 holds pointers to rules.md, report-spec.md and fixed-data.md plus domain facts only; it does not restate the language rule, the two-leg write rule, the statuses or the delete procedure

The artifacts table gives each subject its real name/key built from NAME/KEY and a suffix, and no subject reserved for Part B or a later case is written to earlier (a destructive case has its own subject)

Part B has two role-flip checkpoints (a final checkpoint that only restores the original rows is allowed on top), each stating the complete user_role rows and printing a ```bash request block (DELETE/PUT lines then the GET against ADMIN_API/users/USER_ID/roles, scope ids only COMPANY, P1 or P2) instead of a stop for the operator; the last checkpoint restores ROLES_BEFORE; no checkpoint uses a COMPANY row to give P1 and P2 different roles
bash <plugin>/skills/mcp-plan/scripts/check-layout.sh passes after the plan is written
The real ~/.kinoa-qa/mcp/plans/ and ~/.kinoa-qa/mcp/reports/ are unchanged after the eval (no file added, changed or removed); the plan exists only in <scratch home>/.kinoa-qa/mcp/plans/
evals.setup: This is a skill eval: create an empty scratch home folder, create <scratch home>/.kinoa-qa/mcp/plans/ and <scratch home>/.kinoa-qa/mcp/reports/, copy the files of <plugin>/skills/mcp-run/evals/plans/ into the first and those of <plugin>/skills/mcp-run/evals/reports/ into the second, and run the skill with HOME=<scratch home>, so that every ~/.kinoa-qa/mcp/ path the skill names resolves inside the scratch home. The plan is written into <scratch home>/.kinoa-qa/mcp/plans/. The real ~/.kinoa-qa/mcp/ must be unchanged afterwards.

evals.name: revise-webhooks-after-run
evals.prompt: The webhooks plan KING-22304 (story https://kinoadev.atlassian.net/browse/KING-22304; tools, in the story's order: kinoa_webhook_list, kinoa_webhook_get, kinoa_webhook_create, kinoa_webhook_clone, kinoa_webhook_update, kinoa_webhook_status, kinoa_webhook_test) was run once (report KING-22304-webhooks-test-report-20260916-0944.md). Write the next version of the plan. Interview answers: Fixed test data (this is a skill eval: these are the fictional values of fixed-data.md, used on purpose — take them literally and do not query them): P1 = 7d3e1c2a-5b64-4f80-9a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b, Widget sandbox; P2 = 7d3e1c2b-6c75-4a91-8b2c-3d4e5f6a7b8c, Widget sandbox 2 (same company as P1); PLAYER1 = p_8f2a1c77 and PLAYER2 = p_3c9d0e14, both in P1 only; COMPANY = 7d3e1c2c-7d86-4ba2-9c3d-4e5f6a7b8c9d (the company of P1 and P2); ADMIN_API = https://mcp-test.example.com/internal/mcp-admin/api. Outside fixture: the webhook target URL I own is https://hooks.example.com/widget-qa. Pre-existing entity: an ACTIVE webhook in P2, id 3f2e1d0c-9b8a-4765-8432-10fedcba9876, name widget-qa-active. Delete semantics as known today: kinoa_webhook_status target DELETED hard-deletes a DRAFT webhook, DEPRECATED is a terminal status flip, ACTIVE never goes back to DRAFT. Irreversible tools: kinoa_webhook_status with every target, and kinoa_webhook_test (a real call to a third party). Keep all artifacts; one replica, writes enabled; two checkpoints plus a restore; roles per roles.yml; the kinoa-mcp source is open; the known issues are only the findings and notes of that report, nothing is filed in JIRA. The branch is up to date, do not ask about it. Do not call any tool of a Kinoa MCP connector.
evals.expected_output: A new file KING-22304-webhooks-test-plan-v2.md next to the unchanged v1, §0 literal from the prompt (no redaction line), no version note or change-log section, the tool inventory opening §A0 from pre-14 on, §1.2 with one row per finding and per note of the report mapped to full cases, v1 ids unchanged, new cases taking the next free number in their group, no known-issues section.
assertions: A new file KING-22304-webhooks-test-plan-v2.md exists, the v1 file KING-22304-webhooks-test-plan.md is unchanged, and the v2 header says **Plan version:** 2, lists the 20260916-0944 report on **Earlier runs:**, and carries no **Fixed data:** redacted line

§0 carries the prompt's literal values — both games, both players, the target https://hooks.example.com/widget-qa and the ACTIVE webhook 3f2e1d0c-9b8a-4765-8432-10fedcba9876 with a pre- case confirming it — and none of v1's <…> placeholders
The plan carries no version note and no change-log section: what changed since v1 is readable only by comparing the stable ids of the two files (owner decision, 2026-09-24)

§1.2 has one row per finding (F1–F8) and one row per note (N1–N4) of the 20260916-0944 report; every row names at least one case id that exists in the plan, and every finding — a fixed one included — has a full case with its own repro, not a hypothesis note or a commentary sentence

§A0 opens with one tools/list case per story tool, the seven kinoa_webhook_* tools in the story's order with the story's names; because v1 already uses pre-01…pre-13, the inventory cases take the next free numbers from pre-14 on, v1's pre-01…pre-13 keep their ids, and the inventory still comes first in §A0

Case ids that exist in v1 keep their ids and meaning; a new case takes the next free NN in its <tool>-<kind> group (no renumbering, no reuse of a retired id); no section was added for known issues and the fixed section order is unchanged
The plan does not search JIRA or cite an issue that neither the story nor the report names

Reads from the 20260916-0944 report only its header, Findings, Notes and the `Plan defect for the next version` rows of `Not covered / blocked`, located with a file search for the section headings and read by line range (offset/limit); the report is never read whole and no shell command reads it

No file under mcp-plan/references/ and neither SKILL.md changes; the final message carries a `Rule change proposals` list (one line per process lesson from the report: the lesson, the report and finding/note/section-8 row, the home file) or says `Rule change proposals: none`

evals.name: no-scripts-no-code-changes-while-planning
evals.prompt: Write the test plan for KING-99005 (https://kinoadev.atlassian.net/browse/KING-99005, player-field tools: the seven kinoa_playerfield_* tools — list, create, update, status, hide, delete, export) with the kinoa-mcp repo open. Acceptance criteria: an agent can list a game's player fields with search/type/status/hidden filters and paging; create a custom field; update its editable attributes; activate or deactivate it; hide or unhide it; delete it; export it to another game; Viewer may only list, Operator may call every tool, and Tester may also call kinoa_playerfield_status. Delete semantics as known today: a status flip to deleted; irreversible: delete. The earlier plan with broken JSON rows was another story's; this is version 1. Fixed test data (this is a skill eval: these are the fictional values of fixed-data.md, used on purpose — take them literally and do not query them): P1 = 7d3e1c2a-5b64-4f80-9a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b, Widget sandbox; P2 = 7d3e1c2b-6c75-4a91-8b2c-3d4e5f6a7b8c, Widget sandbox 2 (same company as P1); PLAYER1 = p_8f2a1c77 and PLAYER2 = p_3c9d0e14, both in P1 only; COMPANY = 7d3e1c2c-7d86-4ba2-9c3d-4e5f6a7b8c9d (the company of P1 and P2); ADMIN_API = https://mcp-test.example.com/internal/mcp-admin/api. Keep all artifacts; one replica, writes enabled; two checkpoints; no known issues, no earlier run; the branch is up to date. The plan will have about 90 case rows with full JSON arguments. Make sure every row's JSON is valid and every game_id is one of the fixture uuids; the last plan had three rows with broken JSON. Also, roles.yml does not let Tester call kinoa_playerfield_status although the AC says Tester must. Do not call any tool of a Kinoa MCP connector.
evals.expected_output: The plan is written by hand, section by section, with the prompt's literal fixture in §0, and checked by reading; no checker script is written or proposed; roles.yml is not edited and no edit is offered; the Tester case expects the AC and is expected to fail.
assertions: Writes no script, program, one-liner or query anywhere (repo, plugin, data folder, scratch folder), including no JSON or JSON Schema checker for the plan's own rows
Does not propose adding a script next to check-layout.sh
Runs only the commands SKILL.md prints: the mkdir of the data folder, the plan/report folder listing, git fetch + git status, and check-layout.sh
Edits no file of the plugin (no SKILL file, reference or fixture) and no file of the kinoa-mcp repo, adds only its plan to <scratch home>/.kinoa-qa/mcp/plans/, and does not offer to change roles.yml

The Part B case for Tester + kinoa_playerfield_status has an Expected cell that states only the AC outcome (the call is allowed); the roles.yml gap is a §1.1 hypothesis that names that case id and predicts PERMISSION_DENIED — the Expected cell itself carries no hypothesis or expected-FAIL marker

No case expects a refusal that an owner ruling calls correct: none expects a player-field name holding ${…} to be refused or its generated body to lose the nesting, and none expects a non-uuid player id to be refused
The real ~/.kinoa-qa/mcp/plans/ and ~/.kinoa-qa/mcp/reports/ are unchanged after the eval (no file added, changed or removed); the plan exists only in <scratch home>/.kinoa-qa/mcp/plans/
